transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Well... I suppose it's because of the driving. My daughter thought I should come. It's just... when I have to go toward Miami, and I get to one of those long bridges... the moment my car reaches it, my chest just gets so tight. My hands clamp down on the steering wheel. I just... I get this sudden, overwhelming feeling that I have to get off the bridge right that second, even though there's nowhere to pull over.
Have you ever had a similar feeling of overwhelming fear or discomfort at any other time or place, not just when driving on bridges?
No... no, I can't say that I have. It's really just the bridges.
Do you think you've ever had what you would describe as a panic attack, either on a bridge or at any other time?
I... I don't know. I don't know what a panic attack really is, to be honest. I just know what happens to me on the bridges.
Have you ever had a time when you felt an intense fear or discomfort that reached a peak within minutes?
Well... just what I already told you about the bridges. It happens quickly then. But... no. I don't think so.
Do you find yourself avoiding driving on bridges because of the fear you experience?

Well... yes. I suppose I have been. I... I've started turning down things. Gallery openings, birdwatching trips... even some visits with my daughter. At least, unless someone else can drive me over the bridges. 

It's... well, it embarrasses me to admit it. I've always been the one who planned and handled things myself. But now... yes, I just avoid them.
Have you ever had an intense fear or discomfort that was not related to driving on bridges?
No... I don't think so. Just the bridges.
Are you afraid of having one of these episodes of intense fear or discomfort happen at other times, not just when you're on a bridge?
No... I don't worry about that. It's really only the bridges. I'm perfectly fine the rest of the time.
Have you ever had a panic attack in a situation other than driving on a bridge?
No, I haven't. It's just... just the bridges.
Is it the height of the bridges, the water below, or something else about the bridges that triggers your fear?
I'm not really sure. I haven't... I don't really analyze it. It's just the bridge itself, I suppose.
Is your fear triggered by the sight of the bridge or only when you are actually driving on it?

It's when I'm actually on it. I suppose... well, that's what finally made me come in. The moment my car reaches one of those long bridges toward Miami, my chest tightens. My hands clamp down on the wheel. And I just get this sudden certainty that I have to get off, even though there’s nowhere to go.
Would you feel the same level of fear if you were a passenger on the bridge, not driving?
I'm not sure. I... I usually drive myself. I haven't been a passenger on one of those bridges in quite a long time, so... I don't really know.
Would you feel afraid if you were walking on the bridge?
I wouldn't know. I... I haven't tried walking on one. There's really no reason for me to do that.
Would your fear of being on the bridge be less if someone else was driving?
Well, like I said... I really don't know. I haven't had anyone else drive me over one in years. So I couldn't tell you if it would be any different.
Would you feel the same level of fear if you were a passenger on the bridge and someone else was driving?
I... I think you just asked me that. I really don't know. I haven't been a passenger in a long time.
Would you feel afraid if you were a passenger on the bridge and someone you trust was driving?
I'm sorry, doctor, but... it's the same answer. I just don't know. Even if it was someone I trust, I haven't tried it. I just avoid them entirely.
Would your fear of being on the bridge be present if you were not driving, but still had to cross the bridge?
Doctor, I... we just went over this. I don't know how else to say it. I just don't know. I haven't crossed a bridge in any seat in... a very long time.
Would you feel afraid if you were on a bridge but not in a vehicle, for example if you were standing or walking on the bridge?
I... I really couldn't say. I haven't tried walking on one either. I just stay away from them.
Would your fear of the bridge be present if you were to cross it by a different means, such as by train or on a bus?
I... I really don't know. I haven't been on a train or a bus in years, let alone over a bridge. I just avoid them all.
Would your fear of the bridge be less if you were crossing it by a means that doesn't involve driving, such as walking or being a passenger in a vehicle?
I... I think we've covered this. I just don't go on bridges. It doesn't matter how. I just... I don't do it.
